title: Youngstown dance and getting hired for a carnival
summary: A five-dollar dance gig in Youngstown led to a party where Roy played Hawkins's Stampede chorus and was offered a job with a carnival band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Then we finally got a gig. Some guy wanted the band to go to Youngstown to play a dance, you know. And the money was nice. I guess it must have been about five dollars each. That was nice then, you know. Heh... He said, "Do you fellows want anything to eat before you go?" So the cats said, "Yeah, we'll have a sandwich or something." So we ate big hot dogs and we got bottles of Lehigh soda (back then they called them "pop" I think), and I had me three of those big hot dogs and two bottles of Lehigh. And when we get to the gig, I'm so full, I can't hit a note! All night I was fixing my valves, you know... But we got paid.
Then we got hooked up with another show there that was

playing, like, Youngstown and some other little town close by. You know, you leave towns close enough to (?). That's where I got my good gig. I hooked up with this chick, man; we were supposed to be married, I guess. And she was a (?) on a carnival. Well, (?) we hooked up with her. And she was going with the guy that owned the hotel. And they were giving a party for these people on the carnival. So she had asked us to play for it. Well, naturally, man, we had been playing. And all these musicians there, 42(?) pieces... They had us play "Stampede," and had me play Coleman Hawkins' chorus on "Stampede." Now, that's way back in the Twenties, right? And they said, "I don't believe this. I don't believe this kid, man!" -- and right away, they gave me a job.
